A: Left panel of compound figure shows standing child from back with axillary webbing; caption attributes axillary pterygia to Patient 10 with Escobar/MPS in MPS scoliosis case series. B: Middle panel shows lower limbs with posterior knee webbing; caption attributes popliteal pterygia to Patient 10 with MPS. C: Right panel shows inguinal webbing; caption states inguinal pterygia in Patient 10 with MPS. No vocabulary key for inguinal pterygium, so recorded as proposed finding; panel visibly shows MPS manifestation.

in_text_mentions: Characteristic phenotypic features of Escobar were observed in all 12 patients, including webbing over the neck, axillary, elbow, knee and/or fingers (Table 1). Downslanting palpebral fissures were observed in 10 patients (Table 2). Three patients had cleft palate and another five had high palate. Four patients had both posterior rotated ears and low-set ears, whereas another three patients either had posterior rotated ears or low-set ears. Figure 2 and Figure 3 showcase pterygia and characteristic features in MPS among two patients.

plate_findings.evidence: Posterior-anterior supine film at 10 years old, demonstrating 15° right thoracic and 18° left lumbar curves

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: PA spine radiograph of Patient 10 with compound heterozygous CHRNG variants in MPS article showing thoracic and lumbar scoliotic curves. B: Lateral spine radiograph same MPS patient at 10y showing sagittal spinal deformity as part of scoliosis spectrum described in caption. C: PA sitting spine film same MPS patient at 12y showing progressed moderate 28-degree scoliosis. D: Lateral sitting spine film same MPS patient showing persistent sagittal deformity with measurement overlays, part of described scoliosis progression.
panels.attribution_text: Dahan-Oliel et al. The Clinical and Genotypic Spectrum of Scoliosis in Multiple Pterygium Syndrome: A Case Series on 12 Children.. Genes 2021. doi:10.3390/genes12081220. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 6.
panels.figure_caption: Patient 10 has compound heterozygous CHRNG variants, and a moderate scoliosis, first identified during infancy. (A) Posterior-anterior supine film at 10 years old, demonstrating 15° right thoracic and 18° left lumbar curves, and lateral view (B) Showing mild thoracic hypokyphosis and hip flexion contractures driving lumbar hyperlordosis. At this size, the curves would be considered mild. (C,D) Posterior-anterior and lateral sitting spine films at 12 years of age, showing that the curve had mildly progressed to 28°, reaching criteria for a moderate curve. The sagittal profile continues to show mild thoracic hypokyphosis.
in_text_mentions: oth detected during the first year of life. Both were left sided curves, one a thoracolumbar curve with hyperkyphosis and hypolordosis, the other a lumbar curve with thoracic hypokyphosis. One patient underwent serial casting at 2 years of age, while the curve of the other did not progress past 25° until 12 years of age, and therefore was not treated. Two patients, 5 and 8 years of age at last follow up, had mild curves. They both had a forward lean on the standing sagittal radiographs with flexed hips and mild lumbar hyperlordosis. Figure 6 shows spine X-rays of a child with a moderate curve.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (a, b, c, d, e, f). a: Case 1 frontal fetus view captioned with elbow/knee contractures and clubfoot in lethal multiple pterygium syndrome article; in-text Fig.1a-c with contractures and elbow pterygium. b: Lateral view case 1 captioned with elbow/knee contractures; in-text contractures in elbows, hip and knees with pterygium in elbows (Fig.1a-c) in lethal MPS. c: Close-up upper body/face captioned Note cystic hygroma (c) and part of Fig.1a-c showing contractures with elbow pterygium in lethal MPS; cystic hygroma kept as proposed finding. d: Frontal view case 2 captioned with elbow/knee contractures; in-text cystic hygroma, contractures with elbow pterygium (Fig.1d-f) in lethal MPS. e: Lateral view case 2 captioned with elbow/knee contractures in lethal MPS context. f: Close-up elbow explicitly captioned as pterygium in elbows in fetus with lethal multiple pterygium syndrome.

panels.figure_caption: Frontal and lateral view of case 1 and 2. Contracture in elbows and knees are evident in both foetuses (a, b, d, e), clubfeet is evident in case 1 (a). Note cystic hydromel (c). Pterygium is evident in the elbows (f)
in_text_mentions: ted and the foetus and placenta were undertaken for post-mortem and cytogenetic studies. The foetus showed cystic hygroma, contractures in the elbows, hip and knees with pterygium in the elbows (Fig. 1a–c). Two cultures were set up from muscle tissue, which revealed normal 46,XX pattern. DNA was extracted from muscle tissue to perform array Comparative Genomic Hybridisation (aCGH) for the detection of chromosomal aberrations. The results indicated no genomic imbalance exceeding 0.5 MB in size.Fig. 1Frontal and lateral view of case 1 and 2. Contracture in elbows and knees are evident in both fo

Case 2 is the product of the second pregnancy of the couple. Ultra-sound examination at 12 weeks gestational weeks reported cystic hygroma and subcutaneous oedema in the skull thorax and abdomen. Pleural ascites and ascites were not seen. Therapeutic abortion was performed at 13 weeks of gestation. Grossly the second foetus showed cystic hygroma, contractures in the elbows, hip and knees with pterygium in the elbows (Fig. 1d–f). DNA was extracted from foetal tissue for molecular studies.
